verdict.rationale: CoreWeave has its own grouping mechanisms that act on many items at once. Node Pools apply one shared configuration (labels, taints, annotations) across any number of Nodes, and the autoscaler scales them as a unit. AI Object Storage bucket lifecycle policies apply expiration actions across a bucket's objects. However, the evidence never documents a general bulk-operation facility (multi-select or batch API calls across arbitrary resources), so delivery is indirect and narrow. Missing for 10: an explicit batch/bulk API or console action across resources, bulk object operations beyond lifecycle rules, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: A Node Pool in CKS represents one or more instances that share a common configuration, such as the same labels, taints, and annotations.
You can deploy multiple Node Pools within a single cluster, where each Node Pool contains any number of Nodes.
CKS supports scaling Node Pools by using the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler, letting you scale CKS Node Pools in response to workload demands for GPU, CPU, or memory resources.
Bucket lifecycle policies is the reference for supported lifecycle actions (Expiration, NoncurrentVersionExpiration, AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload)
